action.title: SCALE UP acquisition budget
action.detail: The model's budget posture is still to scale up acquisition: the long-run uptrend is intact, and this kind of phase has historically been when spending to win new and returning users paid back best, especially among active traders. The next few days call for care in applying it: price is about 6% under its 50-day average, Monday's close was the lowest in 30 days, the mood fell to 26 out of 100, and the safety story around exchanges is still running. So add spend only in small steps, lead with safety and trust rather than hard offers, keep part of the increase ready to pause, and speed up only once price wins back about $81,919. This is a budget-timing guide for the business, not trading advice.

reasons: BTC ($77,147) is about 5% above its 200-day average ($73,163), which is still rising.

watch: The long-run trend still points up, but price sits only about $330 above its 30-day low while the mood turns more fearful. A close above $78,500 would steady things, while a close below $76,816 puts the $73,163 average in focus.
analysis: Bottom line: the long-run uptrend still holds, but the short term has weakened and is close to turning down. Short term is soft to neutral: Bitcoin has closed under its 50-day average for 13 days, sits about 6% below it and about 10% under its 30-day high, and Monday's close of $76,816 was the lowest in 30 days. The mood worsened too, with Fear & Greed down to 26 from 37 a day earlier, even though Binance says it paid its loss from its own funds. A normal week now swings about $2,854, so a close above $78,500 (top of a typical week's swing) would turn it clearly up, a close below $76,816 (the 30-day low) would turn it down, and in between it stays choppy. A clean Binance reserve check on 4 November would help, while another exchange incident would hurt, so keep leading with trust rather than offers.

The next month is mixed. The 90-day numbers still point up, with price about 19% higher and about 86% of those days closing above the long-term average, but the last 30 days are down about 11%. Price must win back $81,919 (the 50-day average) for the month to firm up, and only above $86,603 (the 90-day high) is there room to climb further; while it stays under that average, the month keeps fading. US midterm voting ends today, the US jobs report is due on 6 November, and the next Fed meeting is 8 December. Save bigger campaign pushes for that reclaim.

The 3-6 month picture still leans up at a moderate strength, though the cushion is thinner. Price is about 5% above its 200-day average and that average is still rising, about 4% over 90 days, while Bitcoin remains about 38% below its all-time high. The recovery stays intact while price holds above $73,163 (the 200-day average); if that goes, $67,673 (the 200-week average) is the next floor, and $124,753 (the all-time high) stays the far marker. Work on tokenized shares at the New York Stock Exchange is a small plus for the long run, and a close below the 200-day average is what would weaken this picture and be the moment to move budget toward keeping existing users.

items.why: Binance's founder says the roughly $6.3 billion loss was paid from the company's own funds with no borrowing, and its next reserve snapshot is on 4 November. Brazil's Mercado Bitcoin puts its own incident at about $38 million, says about $11 million is frozen and that customers will not lose money. Bloomberg reports Binance raised rebates for smaller market makers to keep trading deep, and the Liquid network says its Bitcoin reserves are fully restored.

new_listings.scope: The first 10 assets on Reku's New Listings tab (reku.id/markets), in the order shown there. Only developments from the last 7 days that come with a source are written up; for the others, the line below says what was found.

items.name: COTI
items.update: COTI went live on Uphold, a fiat on-ramp the project says serves more than 10 million users. On 29 Oct the project also took part in Mozilla Festival 2026, a gathering on privacy and digital rights. Both are the project's own statements.

items.name: Midnight
items.update: Midnight is again highlighting its partnership with Sig Network (2 Nov), which the project says brings private transactions to Ethereum apps without bridging or wrapping assets. It also demoed its Midnight Passport at TOKEN2049 (29 Oct).

items.name: Re
items.update: According to the project, its head of underwriting told The Insurer that Re has raised about $200 million and written $350 million of insurance business this year. Re also said it holds no assets on Binance, paused reUSD redemptions on 29 Oct as a precaution and resumed them on 30 Oct.

items.name: Babylon
items.update: Babylon announced the Bedrock × Babylon vault, which the project says lets native Bitcoin serve as DeFi collateral without wrapping or bridging (details "coming soon"), and refreshed its testnet app for Bitcoin-backed borrowing.

items.name: Pons
items.update: Pons fell about 11% in 24 hours and about 16% over seven days. Its recent posts and PANews give no reason for the fall; the latest posts are routine promotion of fee claims and token launches.

items.name: DODO
items.update: DODO said it is working with Binance to block addresses linked to the hack from using its services, and told market makers and liquidity providers exposed to the affected assets to review their positions.

also.text: offers confidential GPU compute through an OpenAI-compatible API with Foundry, the project says (29 Oct).

quiet.text: Only joke posts in the last week, last on 30 Oct, and no news; it is down about 21% over seven days with no stated reason.

One teaser post on 31 Oct and no news.

items.headline: CZ: Binance Covered Theft Losses With Its Own Balance Sheet, No Borrowing or Asset Sales
items.why: Binance's founder says the loss was paid from the company's own funds with no gap left, which eases worry about the largest exchange; this is the company's side of the story, and its next reserve check is on 4 November.

items.headline: Brazil's Mercado Bitcoin Says It Will Bear the $40 Million Loss From Hack
items.why: A second exchange theft within days keeps the safety worry alive, though it is far smaller, the exchange says customers will not lose money, and it reports about $11 million frozen.

items.headline: SEC Adds Crypto Asset FAQs: Broad Governance Participants Generally Not Centralized Entities
items.why: New staff answers from the top US market regulator give crypto projects clearer guidance on how they are classified, though this is staff guidance and not a law.

items.headline: New Jersey Withdraws Lawsuit Against Coinbase's Staking Business
items.why: One more US state dropped its case over earning rewards on held coins, which removes a legal overhang on that service, according to a Coinbase lawyer.

items.headline: Crypto.com to Shut Down Hong Kong Consumer App Next February
items.why: A global exchange leaving ordinary users in one regulated market shows how costly licensed retail business can be, though its Hong Kong license application for institutions continues.

items.headline: NYSE Taps Wall Street Giant Broadridge to Provide On-Chain Shareholder Voting for Tokenized Stocks
items.why: The world's largest stock exchange is building shareholder records and voting for shares in token form, another step toward mainstream markets using this technology.

summary.short: Binance's statement that it covered the loss itself is offset by the confirmed loss at Mercado Bitcoin, so news is neutral for the week.
summary.medium: Clearer SEC staff guidance and a dropped US state lawsuit slightly outweigh Crypto.com leaving Hong Kong's consumer market.
summary.long: The NYSE's work on share voting for tokenized stocks is a small positive for mainstream use.
